summary: A phase distribution accounts for every phase ENTRY in the sample printed beside it: one per phase a trial is posted under, plus one for each trial posted under none. It tallies entries and not trials, so the sum exceeds the sample whenever a trial is posted under two phases. Phaseless trials count as N/A, the answer phaseDisplay already gives them, so summary and rendered rows agree; that bucket is lossy and Trial.Phases keeps empty distinguishable from ["NA"]. All four commands compute this through one helper, tallyPhases. The country list a report prints obeys the same per-entry rule, since geo ranges over Trial.Countries while sponsor reads one scalar. Not the empty-distribution case phase-key-always-present-on-trial-shaped-json covers.
reason: Each tally ranged over t.Phases unguarded, so observational trials entered no bucket and vanished — a live compare summed 255 against a sample_size of 300. The guard then existed as four identical copies, only one reachable from a test, so the rule that they agreed lived in an argument rather than in code. report assembled its view inside RunE behind a live client, so nothing could assert it reached the helper at all.
validated_outcome: A fixture must carry each tallied field at zero, one and more than one; one where every trial has exactly one phase cannot separate a per-trial tally from a per-entry one. buildTopicReport takes the fetched sample and returns the briefing, so report is reachable without a client. Negating the phaseless guard fails tests in three files at once, which is what shows no caller kept a private loop. compare and emerging still tally inside RunE behind a live client. Guarded by TestPhaseTallyCountsEveryPhaseEntry, TestTallyPhasesCountsEntriesNotTrials, TestBuildTopicReportCountsPhaseEntries and TestBuildTopicReportCountsEverySite.
